steps.desc: An “urgent” message from the CEO lands in your inbox. Every choice you make changes how the story ends.
steps.intro: Your call this time. You’ll face three decisions, and each one changes how the story plays out. There’s more than one ending.

scenes.title: Inbox
scenes.tip: An urgent email from the CEO. What do you do?

msgs.text: URGENT. I’m in a board meeting. Buy 5 × $100 gift cards for a client and send me the codes within 10 minutes. Don’t call, I can’t talk.

choices.text: Buy the gift cards right away. It’s the CEO!

effects.out: The codes are gone within minutes. The “CEO” was a scammer using a lookalike domain.

choices.text: Reply to the email and ask if it’s really them.

effects.out: The scammer replies “Yes it’s me, hurry!”. Replying in the same thread only reaches the attacker.

choices.text: Check the sender address, then call the CEO’s office on the known number.

effects.out: The address is cyberquest-corp.co, not cyberquest.co. The CEO’s assistant confirms it isn’t real.

scenes.title: SMS
scenes.tip: Now they’re pushing harder. How do you respond?

msgs.text: Why is this taking so long? Do it NOW or there will be consequences. – Daniel

choices.text: Give in. Pressure from the top is too risky to ignore.

effects.out: Urgency and threats are classic pressure tactics. Real leaders don’t demand secret gift card codes.

choices.text: Report it with the Report Phishing button and tell Security.

effects.out: Security blocks the sender and the lookalike domain for the whole company within minutes.

choices.text: Ignore it and get back to work.

effects.out: You’re safe, but nobody else is warned. The same message is still hitting other inboxes.

scenes.title: Team chat
scenes.tip: A colleague needs help. What do you tell Rafi?

msgs.text: Hey, I got the same email this morning and already sent the codes… was that bad?

choices.text: Tell Rafi not to worry about it.

effects.out: The stolen codes are already being spent. The sooner it’s reported, the better the chance to stop it.

choices.text: Help Rafi report it to Security and Finance right away.

effects.out: Finance contacts the gift card provider fast enough to freeze most of the codes.

choices.text: Forward the scam email to the whole team as a warning.

effects.out: Good intent, but forwarding spreads the malicious message. Report it and share a screenshot through official channels instead.

best.title: Threat contained
best.text: You verified, reported and helped a colleague act fast. The scam went nowhere.

mid.title: Close call
mid.text: Some good instincts, but a few gaps let the scam spread. See if you can find the best ending.

bad.title: The scam paid off
bad.text: Pressure won this time. Lookalike domains plus urgency is the oldest trick in the book. Try another path.

debrief.headline: Story complete!
debrief.sub: Every path teaches something. Here’s how your choices played out.

meta.description: Three tense moments, three choices each: keep security and trust high.
